title: polling-cost run manifest
description: The single line at the head of a pass, carrying the environment once rather than on every record. Every field is a condition of the numbers below it: a figure without them is an estimate wearing a decimal point.

run_tag.description: The tag this pass was written under. A re-measurement writes a new tag beside the pass it is compared with; nothing is edited in place.

git_rev.description: The commit the measured tree was at.

git_dirty.description: Whether the MEASURED tree — crates/ and the workspace manifests — had uncommitted changes. Scoped to what was measured rather than to the whole worktree: what makes a number irreproducible is the library moving under it, not this directory gaining a paragraph. A committed pass must carry false.

ram_bytes.description: Total physical RAM in bytes, or 0 where the OS did not say. It is asked for per platform — MemTotal in /proc/meminfo, sysctl -n hw.memsize, Get-CimInstance Win32_ComputerSystem — so zero means the query was made and went unanswered, never that nobody asked. Zero is unknown rather than none, and the README says so rather than the field pretending.

features.description: The feature set the measured crate was built with.

started_at.description: The wall-clock instant THIS RUN started, read from the system clock as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Not the instant of the commit git_rev names: two passes taken months apart at the same revision differ here and nowhere else, so a field reporting the commit instant would make additive re-runs indistinguishable.
